t: Chenla is a Chinese label: most historians now hold that it was never a unitary kingdom but a series of loose and temporary confederations of Khmer principalities, Michael Vickery's 'Dângrêk Chieftains'.

Isanavarman I, whose embassy reached the Sui court in 616–17 and whose capital was Isanapura (Sambor Prei Kuk), absorbed the territories of Funan and called himself King of Kings ruling 'Suvarnabhumi as far as the sea'.
After 707 the Tang histories divide Chenla into Land and Water Chenla; Water Chenla fell to the Javanese around 790, while from Land Chenla Jayavarman II proclaimed the Khmer Empire in 802.
dyk: Judith Jacob found fourteen categories of slaves in Chenla's inscriptions, distinguished by origin and duty; they could be bought, sold and given away, bound by their parents' debts or born into bondage.
ev: On 13 April Narasimhagupta, vassal of Bhavavarman I, erects a figure of Vishnu at Isanapura; the same year Bhavavarman builds a temple at the centre of his kingdom of Bhavapura.
Isanavarman I sends the first Chenla embassy to the Sui court; the Sui annals of 636 are the oldest Chinese text to name Chenla.
Chenla subdues Funan; the New Book of Tang credits Isanavarman with annexing its territory at the beginning of the Zhenguan era.
On 14 June Jayavarman I, son of Candravarman, issues his earliest inscriptions; his reign of about thirty years is the last over a united Chenla.
After the end of the Shenlong era the Tang histories record Chenla divided into Land Chenla (Wendan) and Water Chenla.
On 5 April Queen Jayadevi, ruling at Angkor, complains of 'bad times' in her Western Baray inscription as the kingdom breaks into principalities.
The last king of Water Chenla is killed and his realm absorbed into the Javanese monarchy; Jayavarman II and Indrayudha defeat a Cham army and found Hariharalaya.
Jayavarman II proclaims the Khmer Empire, ending the pre-Angkor period.

f.capital: Bhavapura (near Thala Barivat) under Bhavavarman I; Isanapura (Sambor Prei Kuk) from about 600; Vat Phou at Champasak by the older accounts
f.founder: Bhavavarman I, recognised as independent ruler at the end of the 6th century; with his brother Citrasena (Mahendravarman) the conqueror of Funan
f.predecessor: Funan, of which Chenla was a vassal and one of the regional centres
f.successor: The Khmer Empire, proclaimed by Jayavarman II in 802; Water Chenla had fallen to the Javanese Shailendras around 790
